purpose: Isolate Hermes API gateway's model-based session-title upgrade from the user-facing chat generation.
classification: upstream behavior probe; synthetic, no owner preference

runtime.provider: synthetic OpenAI-compatible provider bound to loopback

method.comparison: first with auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled=true, then false after gateway restart; title generation otherwise enabled
method.provider_capture: request metadata only: whether prompt matched Hermes title template, streaming flag, message count, roles; no prompt or answer text persisted

results.title_visibility: The API returned session IDs, but the probe did not locate a persisted title row in the queried state database. User-visible API/Open WebUI title behavior is not established by this run.

upstream_source_evidence.implementation: Hermes agent/title_generator.py::maybe_auto_title applies an instant derived title before checking model_upgrade_enabled; false returns without spawning the title upgrade thread.
upstream_source_evidence.upstream_test: tests/agent/test_title_generator.py::test_model_upgrade_disabled_keeps_derived_title_and_spawns_no_thread asserts the derived title remains, and asserts no thread or LLM call. Inspected, not run in this campaign.

interpretation: A titleable first turn with the native model upgrade enabled caused one additional nonstream provider request. Setting model_upgrade_enabled=false removed that request while leaving the main streamed answer successful.
This validates the native call-count effect, not the title's visibility or owner value. The setting is not changed in HADES pending API/UI title-path evidence.
Four nonstream provider posts with empty messages appeared across the two gateway runs. Their purpose was not identified and they are excluded from the title-call comparison.

No live model, production endpoint, owner session, or external service was used. The probe used unmodified Hermes and does not qualify HADES overlay, Open WebUI, production latency, or user preference.
